newsitem.title: USA: Don't interfere with CRP renewal--USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Don't interfere with CRP renewal--USDA's Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman urged the U.S. Congress to resist proposals to cap new enrollment in the Conservation Reserve and to let farmers unilaterally extend their contracts for a year.
"We hope they can resist both of these," Glickman told the National Association of Agricultural Journalists.
So far, he noted, the proposals have support only among House members. If adopted, he said, they would hobble renewal of the Conservation Reserve and keep healthy land out of use.
"That path could very well put us in the position of having to import more grain from Canada," he said.
Canadian wheat imports are a sore issue in the U.S. Wheat Belt.
Glickman said either of the proposals would make it difficult to bring fragile land into the reserve, which pays farmers an annual rent to idle land for 10 years.
"It would be a mistake to put this program on hold for a year," he told the NAAJ annual meeting.

As in the past, Glickman said USDA would notify farmers "by the end of May -- on time" if their land would be accepted for enrollment. Farmers offered 25.6 million acres during a sign-up last month. Contracts of more than 21 million acres expire this fall. USDA has said it might enroll up to 19 million acres.
